review.tagline: Translates scientific PDFs while keeping formulas, figures and layout intact
review.summary: pdf2zh translates scientific PDFs and writes a translated-only and a bilingual (dual) PDF, preserving formulas, charts, table of contents and annotations. It runs as a CLI, a Gradio web UI on port 7860, a Python or HTTP API, or an MCP server, and calls a configurable translation service (Google by default). Layout detection uses a DocLayout-YOLO ONNX model, with optional OCR and an --ultrafast mode.
review.audience: Researchers and self-hosters translating academic PDFs
strengths: Outputs both translated-only and side-by-side bilingual PDFs from one command
Many interfaces: CLI, Gradio GUI, Docker, Python API, HTTP API, MCP stdio/SSE
Selectable translation backends via -s, with Google as the default
Optional OCR for scanned pages and --ultrafast mode for native-text PDFs
weaknesses: OCR is experimental and targets white-background scans; handwriting may fail
Last release is 2025-07-11; v2 work lives in a separate PDFMathTranslate-next repo
--ultrafast is CLI fast mode only and is weaker on complex tables or formulas
needs: Needs DocLayout-YOLO ONNX model (Hugging Face download), Translation service (Google default, others configurable)
